lines.text: Your fingers wrinkle in water, and it is not swelling!
Skin doesn't puff up like a sponge. Your nervous system does this on purpose!
After a few minutes in water, your nerves squeeze the tiny blood vessels under your fingertips,
and the skin gets pulled inward, so the wrinkles pop out.
Here is the proof. People with a damaged finger nerve don't wrinkle at all!
So why would your body bother? One theory says they work like tire treads.
The grooves channel water away, so your grip sticks to wet things.
In a two thousand thirteen test, people with wrinkled fingers moved wet marbles faster!
But a later study in Berlin found no difference. Scientists still argue about it.
So are wrinkly fingers a built-in grip upgrade, or just a strange side effect?
